1. (S) SITUATION:
A crippled British destroyer, HMS Sheffield, is broadcasting distress near Bear Island. Intelligence assesses that the transmission may be bait intended to draw {TaskForceName} into a prepared submarine ambush. The destroyer may also be carrying NATO's senior anti-submarine warfare coordinator for the Norwegian Sea.
2. (S) MISSION: 2.1 Locate and destroy HMS Sheffield. 2.2 Neutralise the submarine ambush. 2.3 {FlagshipName} must survive.
3. (S) EXECUTION: 3.1 Approach the distress position with sensors active and maintain an anti-submarine screen. 3.2 Confirm the disposition of Sheffield before committing the main force. 3.3 Destroy the ambushing submarines and the destroyer if the tactical picture permits. 3.4 Break contact if the force becomes fixed or the flagship is threatened.
4. (S) ENEMY SITUATION: 4.1 HMS Sheffield is damaged and may be unable to maneuver. 4.2 At least two NATO attack submarines are assessed near the distress position.
5. (S) FRIENDLY SITUATION: 5.1 {TaskForceName} is assigned to investigate and exploit the opportunity. 5.2 The task force's submarines and helicopters are the primary anti-submarine assets.
6. (S) INTEL ASSESSMENT: 6.1 The distress call is likely intended to trigger a predictable Soviet response. 6.2 Destruction of Sheffield and the ambush force may remove a senior NATO anti-submarine coordinator from the theater. The intelligence value justifies a controlled risk, not reckless exposure of the flagship.
